title: Release Windowing and Triage Grid for Hosted API Model Catalog — Q3 Planning
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable, low-risk quarterly release cadence for Hosted API model updates that balances time-to-ship with observability and rollback safety. We will produce: 1) a release windowing policy (calendar + guardrails), 2) a triage grid that maps regression severity to operations flow, and 3) a lightweight playbook for canary cohorts and automated rollback triggers.

Background: Q2 saw several near-miss regressions when model variants were rotated in close succession. Engineers called for clearer release gates and a predictable cadence to reduce cognitive load. Sales/CS want faster model additions for customers, but infra/ops require stricter SLO preservation. This ticket is the PM-side orchestration to reconcile those constraints and produce an operationally-usable plan for the next quarter.

Scope (in): hosted API model lineup changes (promotes/rotations/deprecations), canary cohort definitions, monitoring/alert thresholds tied to evals, documented rollback flows, required gating signals from Console and runtime metrics.

Scope (out): low-level kernel selection, per-GPU autoscaling configs (ENG to own), and private deployment release mechanics (separate Private playbook).

Key trade-offs considered: 
- Frequency vs. blast radius: Shorter windows enable faster iterations but increase ops churn and noise in metrics.
- Canary cohort size vs. statistical sensitivity: Larger cohorts detect regressions earlier but increase customer exposure.
- Strict automation vs. human-in-the-loop: Auto-rollback reduces MTTR but risks false positives for transient infra noise.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Three-tier release windows: Quick (weekday AM) for low-risk config and minor model parameters; Standard (weekday evening) for candidate model promotions after internal eval pass; Full (Saturday early morning) for major lineup changes and deprecations where cross-team coordination is required.
2) Triage grid: Severity buckets (S1-S4) mapped to concrete actions, owners, SLAs, and rollback thresholds. Example: S1 = global generation failure -> immediate rollback + exec notification; S3 = small latency increase within SLO but sustained >72h -> investigate and schedule patch.
3) Canary cohorts & gating: Define cohort sizes per traffic percentile (1% seed, 10% validation, 100% ramp) with automated metric checks (generation error rate, mean latency p95, quality regression via prompt-specific evals).
4) Runbook + SLA: Short runbook snippets embedded in Console per-release with one-click rollback links and prescriptive postmortem checklist.

Deliverables: release-windowing calendar, triage grid doc, Console checklist UI spec, 3 example rollout schedules for two target models, and a playbook PR with automation knobs (metrics thresholds) for runtime/observability teams.

Acceptance criteria: clear owner for each window, a documented triage grid with example incidents mapped, two successful dry-run releases in staging using the new windows and gating, Console checklist visible to release approvers, and a retention plan for post-release evals for 30 days.

Stakeholders: Product (Lina Chen), Hosting/Serving Runtime (Eng leads: Priya Rao), Console/Observability (Eng leads: Jamal Brooks), Reliability (SRE: Maria Alvarez), Legal/Compliance (for model deprecations affecting customers).

Risks & mitigation:
- False-positive rollbacks from transient infra noise: mitigate by requiring at least two metrics to cross threshold or human confirmation for Full windows.
- Delays from cross-team scheduling: mitigate by pre-authorized weekend windows and a release coordinator rota.
- Customer impact from model behavior regressions: mitigate with shorter initial cohort windows and explicit customer communication templates.

References & artifacts: design spec (drive) and initial dashboard prototypes are linked below. Also see related evaluation harness and example PRs for automation knobs.
